comment: Maps claim_type → applicable rule modules per tribunal. The simulator routes a fact pattern through these mappings: pick claim type + tribunal, fill in inputs for each applicable rule, aggregate the per-rule outputs into a verdict. Each rule entry is a {module, scope} pair into rules/_index.json. The 'role' field tells the simulator how the rule contributes to the verdict (gate / arithmetic / disposition / interpretation). Frequencies after each row are how many corpus judgments code that claim_type.

applicable_rules.when: Standard-basis assessment ordered. Hours allowed × hourly rate + reasonable disbursements.
Indemnity-basis review ordered. Triages each defendant objection into mechanically_disposed / held_to_zero / deterministic_reduction / requires_human_judgment.
DIFC-seated arbitration costs order under PD 4/2017. 80% discretion + 14-day deadline + 9% interest if late.

claim_types.label: Recognition / enforcement of a foreign arbitral award (NY Convention)

applicable_rules.when: Foreign award presented for recognition in Singapore. Defendant pleads grounds under IAA s 31 (NY Convention Art V); court rules on each.
An 'infra petita' natural-justice challenge is pleaded. DKT v DKU four-condition framework applies.
Foreign award presented for recognition in ADGM. Defendant pleads grounds under Arbitration Regulations s 56.

claim_types.label: Enforcement of a foreign arbitral award (post-recognition)

applicable_rules.when: Defendant resists enforcement. Same grounds as recognition.
The contract's meaning is contested. Wood v Capita unitary approach decides between plain meaning, business common sense, or genuine ambiguity.
A liquidated-damages clause is engaged and the claimant seeks payment under it. Court may cap at proportionate amount under Art 390(2) if grossly exaggerated.
One or more contract items are admitted. Court enters judgment for admitted sums minus proven counterclaim sums.
A party seeks to adduce fresh evidence. Three-prong conjunctive test gates admissibility.
Court is asked to give summary judgment under ADGM CPR Rule 24. Conjunctive test: no realistic prospect AND no other compelling reason for trial.
A duty of care is in dispute. Caparo three-stage test: foreseeability + proximity + fair, just, reasonable.

claim_types.label: Interim relief — third-party disclosure / freezing / proprietary injunction

applicable_rules.when: Applicant seeks disclosure against a non-party (typically a financial institution holding traceable proceeds). Three conjunctive jurisdictional gates — Norwich Pharmacal, Bankers Trust, RDC 28.52 — all required.
